newsitem.title: UK: LBMA daily gold volume raises slightly in May.
newsitem.headline: LBMA daily gold volume raises slightly in May.

text.p: Volume of gold's average daily clearing turnover rose slightly in May to 32.4 million ounces from 32.1 million ounces in April, according to data released on Thursday by the London Bullion Market Association.
The value was unchanged from April at $11.1 billion reflecting a slightly lower average for the London afternoon fix of $343.84 down from $344.47.
The number of transfers fell to 1,154 from 1,174 in April.
LBMS chairman Peter Fava said, "The figures show a very steady trend. May was a very quiet month for the maket both in terms of price and volume."
He added that the level of business could be expected to slow during the traditionally quiet period from June through to the end of August.

The average silver daily clearing volume was 236.6 million ounces in May compared with 253.0 million ounces in April and in value terms silver turnover was worth $1.1 billion compared with $1.2 billion in April.
The number of transaction totalled 455 compared with 482 in April.
The average silver price was a cent lower in May at $4.76 per ounce.

"Activity in the bullion market was generally quiet during May with only short bursts of interest and prices were generally stable within the ranges $349.10-$339.25 for gold and $4.87-$4.65 for silver," the LBMA said.
